sentences.text:
THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:10257 CRL.MC NO. 358 OF 2025 2  ORDER

Petitioner's vehicle bearing Registration No.KL 41 S 373 was seized by the police in Crime No.1387 of 2024 registered at the Aluva East Police Station alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 281, 125(a), 125(b) of BNS, 3(1) r/w 181, 146 r/w 196 of the MV Act.
2. The crime was registered on the allegation that on 16.8.2024, petitioner's vehicle met with an accident resulting in the 2nd respondent being injured.
The petitioner was not driving the vehicle when the accident occurred and therefore was not made an accused.
He moved an application for interim custody of the vehicle, which the learned Magistrate granted subject to certain conditions.
The petitioner's grievance is regarding Condition No.1 in Annexure A1, which requires him to furnish cash security of Rs.6 lakhs.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the 2025:KER:10257 reason for imposing deposit of cash security of Rs.6 lakhs is absence of a valid insurance policy for the vehicle on the date of accident.

It is pointed out that the 2 nd respondent has filed an affidavit stating that the entire expenses for his hospitalization and treatment was met by the petitioner and he therefore, has no further claim in connection with the accident.

4. Learned Public Prosecutor submits that the court below was justified in directing the petitioner to deposit cash security as a condition for grant of interim custody since the vehicle was not covered by a valid insurance policy and the compensation, if any, awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal will have to be paid by the owner and the driver.

5. A perusal of Annexure A3 affidavit filed by the 2 nd respondent reveals that, as the petitioner had met the hospitalization and treatment charges by expending an amount of Rs.62,000/-, the 2nd respondent has no further claim against the petitioner.

In his affidavit, the 2 nd respondent has sworn that he 2025:KER:10257 does not intend to prefer any litigation against the petitioner in connection with the accident as he is satisfied with the payment received.
The injured himself having sworn to an affidavit that he does not intend to raise any claim in future, direction to deposit cash security equivalent to the value of the vehicle is unjustified.
The sole purpose of imposing such a condition is to ensure that the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal can be realized from the cash security deposited.
In the case at hand, no such contingency will arise in view of the stand taken by the injured that he has no intention of raising any claim for compensation.
For the aforementioned reasons, the Crl.M.C is allowed by deleting Condition No.1 in Annexure A1 judgment.
